# QS-PROC-03 Ring rolling dimensional control (P1)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
-------
This quality specification defines dimensional control requirements for ring rolling operations at Plant P1, line P1-L2, with emphasis on heat treat integration and final dimensional verification for rings processed on the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03. It applies to production and inspection personnel responsible for rolling, heat treating, and final measurement activities for parts routed through the line. It does not replace process control plans or maintenance procedures; it is intended to be used in conjunction with MM-P1-L2-HT03, SB-1035, and SOP-P1-L2-04.

Background and rationale
------------------------
Dimensional stability of forged rings is controlled by a combination of forming practices and heat treatment. The austenitizing temperature used in the furnace prior to quench and temper has a direct effect on final microstructure and resultant dimensional change during post-heat-treat stabilization. To minimize variability, operators must follow fixed setpoints, documented transfer conditions, and prescribed inspection methods. This specification documents the critical setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and defines inspection and nonconformance handling steps to ensure consistent ring geometry at final inspection. Related maintenance and equipment calibration information is contained in MM-P1-L2-HT03; metallurgical acceptance criteria are referenced in SB-1035; operation sequence and operator actions are specified in SOP-P1-L2-04.

Requirements table
------------------
| Requirement | Acceptance / Instruction | Record to retain |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| Furnace austenitizing setpoint | The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. | Furnace log entry from EQ-P1-L2-HT03 showing setpoint and operator initials; cross-reference to SOP-P1-L2-04 operation step. |
| Post-heat-treat dimensional tolerance verification | Final ring dimensions shall meet drawing requirements as specified on work order; if drawing requires additional metallurgical exceptions, follow SB-1035. | Final inspection report linked to work order and SB-1035 disposition notes. |
| Transfer conditions between rolling and heat treat | Parts must be handled in accordance with SOP-P1-L2-04 to avoid mechanical distortion during transfer. | Transfer checklist signed by sender and receiver. |
| Measurement method and gauge control | Use calibrated gauges referenced to MM-P1-L2-HT03 and recorded per plant gauge control practice. | Calibration certificates and measurement records filed per MM-P1-L2-HT03. |

Inspection method
-----------------
Overview
This section describes the method for verifying ring dimensions after heat treat and prior to shipment. The purpose is to identify dimensional shifts attributable to heat treatment or handling and to document compliance.

Preparation
- Verify the furnace austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 is set as specified in this document prior to processing. Confirm the setpoint entry in the furnace log and sign the process step as required by SOP-P1-L2-04.
- Ensure measuring equipment is within calibration according to MM-P1-L2-HT03. Reject any out-of-calibration gauge before use and notify quality control.

Measurement procedure
- Stabilize the part per the handling instructions in SOP-P1-L2-04 to eliminate residual handling distortion.
- Measure the ring dimensions defined on the drawing using the controlled gauges. Record measured values on the final inspection report field provided on the work order.
- For any dimension approaching drawing limits, perform a secondary verification using an alternative calibrated instrument and document both measurements and operator initials.

Example scenarios and interpretation
- If a measured diameter deviates from the drawing beyond allowable drawing limits, tag the part for nonconformance review and follow the nonconformance handling section below. Record the condition with photographs and measurement records.
- If repeated parts from the same heat exhibit a trend toward the same deviation, stop production and initiate the hold and review process with process engineering, referring to MM-P1-L2-HT03 for furnace checks and SB-1035 for metallurgical assessment.

Records to keep
- Furnace setpoint log for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 showing the austenitizing setpoint entry and operator initials.
- Final inspection report for each part processed through P1-L2 line, including measurement entries and gauge identifiers.
- Transfer checklist between rolling and heat treat, signed by responsible personnel.
- Calibration certificates and evidence of gauge checks per MM-P1-L2-HT03.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records linked to SB-1035 when applicable.

Nonconformance handling
-----------------------
Detection and immediate actions
- When a dimensional nonconformance is detected, isolate affected parts and clearly tag them with a unique hold identifier. Record the finding on the final inspection report and notify quality control immediately.
- If the nonconformance is suspected to be related to heat treatment, suspend further runs to the furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03 pending investigation. Consult MM-P1-L2-HT03 for furnace performance checks and SOP-P1-L2-04 for any operator action history.

Investigation and root cause
- Initiate a documented investigation that reviews furnace setpoint logs for EQ-P1-L2-HT03, transfer checklists, measurement records, and recent maintenance activity. Use SB-1035 for guidance on metallurgical examination when dimensional change could be microstructure related.
- Gather evidence: furnace log showing the austenitizing setpoint, measurement records, handling checklists, and calibration certificates. Preserve sample parts for metallurgical evaluation if required.

Disposition and corrective action
- Determine disposition using SB-1035 criteria for metallurgical acceptance and drawing limits for dimensional acceptance. Document the final disposition on the nonconformance report and link to the work order.
- Implement corrective actions proportionate to root cause. Examples include confirming the austenitizing setpoint on EQ-P1-L2-HT03, reinforcing SOP-P1-L2-04 transfer procedures with operators, or addressing gauge calibration gaps per MM-P1-L2-HT03.
- Record corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification steps. Close the nonconformance once all verification measures confirm compliance.

References
----------
See MM-P1-L2-HT03 for maintenance and calibration requirements; SB-1035 for metallurgical acceptance and test methods; SOP-P1-L2-04 for operation and transfer steps.
